name: RubatoDB
tagline: University of Alberta NewSQL research system: MySQL-compatible, staged grid architecture over Berkeley DB.
description: RubatoDB is a NewSQL database developed by Li-Yan Yuan's group at the University of Alberta together with Shanghai Shifang Software. It presents itself to clients as a MySQL server but spreads table partitions over a grid of commodity machines, built as a staged architecture of modules connected by explicit queues, with Berkeley DB files as the storage layer and its own 'formula' multi-version timestamp protocol on top for distributed concurrency control. Unusually, it lets each transaction choose between full ACID, BASE-style eventual consistency, or an intermediate 'BASIC' level. The team reported TPC-C runs with 3,200 warehouses on 16 servers. The university-hosted source and docs have disappeared and there are no visible recent releases, so it is mainly of research interest.
statusNote: No visible releases in years and the University of Alberta source and documentation pages are gone; rubatodb.com still describes the system.
developer: University of Alberta and Shanghai Shifang Software

pricing.notes: Distributed as a research download; no current public release.

scale.notes: Tables are partitioned over many commodity servers; TPC-C was reported with 3,200 warehouses on 16 nodes.

strengths: Per-transaction choice of ACID, BASE or intermediate 'BASIC' consistency
MySQL-compatible front end over a horizontally partitioned grid
Staged, queue-connected module design is a clear study of SEDA-style DBMS architecture
Full SQL features such as triggers and stored procedures on a distributed store
weaknesses: No current public release, source or documentation from the university
Joins are reported to work only across tables on the same node
Tiny community and little independent benchmarking
useCases: Research on tunable consistency in NewSQL systems
